PUBLIC LAUNCH · V1.0.0-RC.99 · 2026-10-23

RC.99: SMART, RESOURCE-AWARE AUTOINDEX
AND MORE HARNESS TOOLS.

XERJ ENGINEERING · PUBLISHED 2026-10-23

v1.0.0-rc.99 is the public launch. Autoindex in this cut respects the machine it is running on. It drains memtable pressure on the 8 GiB tier, packs embeddings so a JSONL corpus does not keep a number tree in memory, streams or skips an oversized JSON document, and prints a neural embedding estimate before the run starts. The harness gained definition lookup, a search prefix, and matched-line citations, plus a DeepSeek Harness profile bundle and a Cline row that has now been run. It is also the 98th tagged v1.0.0-rc.* release. 97 tags exist through rc.98, because rc.79 was never tagged. It lands just over 100 days since rc.1.

01 · THE MACHINE

Autoindex that stays inside the box you gave it

A laptop and a large server do not get the same budget. Below 64 GiB of effective memory the auto tier is 8 GiB. On that tier the summed memtable budget is 2 GiB (25% of the cap, floored at 2 GiB) while each index still flushes at 512 MiB by default. A corpus spread across dozens of indices crosses the process budget with every index under its own flush line. Writes stay HTTP 429 and the indexed count stays 0. The sampler now requests a drain when that summed-memtable latch is engaged, on the same interval as the RSS latch. A bulk the parent breaker has not accepted a single item from stops at 90 seconds, and the terminal line names limits.max_process_memory_mb (#2244).

8 GiB
auto tier below 64 GiB
The cap the process derives when effective memory is under 64 GiB. 64 GiB and 128 GiB hosts step up to 16 GiB and 32 GiB.
2 GiB
memtable budget on that tier
25% of the 8 GiB cap. Pressure on this sum now drains, so a multi-index corpus can make progress.
8 MiB
one JSON document
Past this ceiling the document is skipped or refused. The ceiling is fixed.
64 MiB
uncompressed JSON, streamed
A file over the old whole-file cap is walked from disk. Gzip still uses the in-memory cap.

Embeddings are packed. A semantic_text vector is stored as one xerj:f32: hex string. GET and _source expand it back to a number array on the page that is returned. kNN and HNSW read the same bits. Both memtables used to keep the JSON number tree until flush, which is what let JSONL autoindex resident memory grow with the corpus (#2240).

One oversized JSON document is streamed or refused. A single document over 8 MiB is not indexed, so one large file does not have to be parsed and tokenized inside one request. Autoindex streams a top-level array, or a top-level array of records, one element at a time, and skips only the values over that ceiling. The skip names the file. A bulk item over the limit is HTTP 413, and its neighbours still index. The ceiling is a fixed constant. It is not raised by --max-file-mb or limits.max_process_memory_mb (#2256).

The node reserves memory for a bulk before it parses one. Before a raw batch is parsed, the engine reserves 28 bytes per input byte against live process memory and against reservations already held, and rechecks the add so two bulks cannot both pass the same snapshot. A batch that would reach the watermark is HTTP 429 circuit_breaking_exception before the WAL append. An uncompressed .json file over 64 MiB is walked from disk, one document-sized value at a time, instead of being refused unread. Gzip stays on the in-memory cap, because the uncompressed length is not known until the bytes are inflated (#2302).

#2256, #2302, and #2236 improve #1122. That issue stays open.

A killed corpus index resumes. A kill after indices exist and before the ledger is written used to re-hash the corpus under a different prefix, and xerj code then said no verified build was recorded. The command now finds that build's journal and resumes it (#2243).

Windows sizes the cap from commit space. The auto tier is still chosen from physical RAM. On Windows a second ceiling then applies: what this process can still reach, min(commit limit, process commit + available commit), minus a reserve of one quarter of that amount, clamped to 512 MiB–2 GiB. A pagefile that covers RAM does not move the 64 GiB and 128 GiB tier steps. The report behind the change is a 16 GiB machine with no pagefile (#2174, #2236). This is part of the same open issue, #1122.

A full disk says so in one sentence. A memory write blocked at the flood-stage watermark used to surface as a nested cluster_block_exception. The client now turns that block into one sentence: the disk holding the data dir is nearly full, with free space, used percent, the threshold, the data-dir path, and the recovery (free space, or restart with --data-dir on another drive). A reason that already says this is left as it is. An explicit index.blocks.write stays the original error (#2290).

Neural embedding time is estimated before the run. When the server has measured a probe, autoindex prints how long embedding the source that feeds a semantic_text dataset should take, from that probe's passages, bytes, and milliseconds. The figure comes from the probe. No probe, a zero probe, or a non-neural backend prints no duration. The same note says --embed-mode is fixed per index at ingest: changing the flag leaves documents already written as they are, and a new index is how you re-embed. The default embedder is lexical feature-hashing unless the node was started with --embed-mode neural (#2250).

index.default_pipeline survives a restart. Create stored the binding in settings.json, and GET /_settings still reported it after a clean restart, but an ordinary document write no longer ran the pipeline. Opening an existing index now copies that file into the in-memory map before the index is visible. Explicit ?pipeline= was already working. index.final_pipeline is not a setting this build reads (#2296).

_refresh no longer stalls behind a merge. The handler used to flush every matching index in turn, including verified WAL maintenance when the memtable was already empty. A wildcard refresh at the end of autoindex sat behind the first index whose durability tail was slow, and a merge encode held a blocking thread for the whole encode. Matching indices now refresh together. An empty memtable returns without that WAL maintenance. A merge encode is queued on the merge pool. A refresh that still has a memtable to publish stays inside the existing flush admission and caller budgets (#2245).

02 · HARNESS TOOLS

Definitions, a prefix, a line number, two clients

MCP xerj_def (#2166) is local definition lookup. It takes symbol, prefix or index, kind, lang, k from 1 to 50, and max_tokens. No match is a successful empty hit list. Invalid arguments are rejected before any HTTP request. With neither prefix nor index, it searches ax-*.

MCP xerj_search accepts prefix (#2137). {"prefix":"project","query":"retry policy"} searches project-*. The default with neither index nor prefix remains ax-*. An empty prefix, a prefix that cannot name an index, or index and prefix together is rejected before HTTP.

A hit can name the matched line. xerj_search used to report only the passage start_line, so an agent citing file:line had to count lines inside the passage. Plain queries now stamp match_line and a capped match_lines on each hit. match_line is the absolute 1-based source line of the best-scoring whole-word query term inside the passage. A tie takes the earliest line. xerj search prints the same annotation as path:match_line. Both fields are omitted when no term is located or the passage start line is unknown. start_line stays the passage start (#2269).

DeepSeek Harness has a profile bundle, and the row is untested. #2298 adds dsh/. It does not start a node and does not replace xerj mcp. It inserts one @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client plugin, with command: xerj so the bundle does not hard-code a machine path. The README's supported-agents table still marks that row untested: the path and shape are transcribed from the client's own documentation, and nobody has run it yet. XERJ is not in a DeepSeek directory.

Cline is marked tested. #2300. Cline CLI 3.0.73 on Linux registered xerj mcp from the README's mcpServers block, against xerj v1.0.0-rc.98. xerj_search appeared in the tool list Cline handed the model, and Cline executed one xerj_search call. The model turn was a local OpenAI-compatible stub, because no provider key was available. The IDE's MCP Servers > Configure button was not part of that run. OpenCode was already the other tested row. The README's definition of tested is that the server was registered and xerj_search appeared in the tool list.

03 · ALSO IN THIS CUT

CPUs without AVX2, the first cluster data-plane steps, one semantic skip

x86_64 binaries no longer require AVX2 (#2253, #2161). The release baseline is x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2: Nehalem and later, Bulldozer and later). The HNSW eight-accumulator dot product is compiled again with AVX2 and FMA enabled and selected at runtime when the CPU has both. The source does not use an explicit FMA, so that compilation is bit-identical to the scalar one. Installers install on a CPU without AVX2. XERJ_SKIP_CPU_CHECK is gone. A CPU without SSE4.2 still cannot run the binary. Field report #2158 is an Intel Core i3-3110M, Ivy Bridge, which has no AVX2.

Cluster replication took its first data-plane steps. #1170 stays open. A single node is unchanged: with no cluster handle, writes and search stay on the node that received them.

  • #2257 proposes index create, delete, mapping, and settings through the Raft log when a cluster handle is attached. The HTTP call succeeds after this node has applied the committed entry. A follower forwards to the leader.
  • #2271 puts one primary per member into that same create entry. Member ids are sorted. GET, PUT, and POST of one document, and DELETE /{index}/_doc/{id}, run on that owner. A search of one concrete index asks every owner.
  • #2287 copies an acknowledged document write onto replicas before the caller is answered. index.number_of_replicas at create places those copies on the next members in the ring, wrapping, never on the primary, and capped at one less than the member count. An absent setting places zero replicas. The bytes live in a hidden index, .xerj_replica_{index}_{shard}, so a search fan-out does not count a document twice.
  • #2303 acknowledges a document write at a majority of the copies placed at create (copies / 2 + 1), and the primary counts. With two replicas, the primary plus one replica is enough. The replica that does not confirm is removed from the in-sync set before the caller is answered. The primary alone, when two replicas were placed, is still HTTP 503 replica_not_acknowledged. Zero or one replica is unchanged: that one replica must still confirm.

What #1170 still requires: there is no wait_for_active_shards and no replica promotion. Changing number_of_replicas after create does not relocate or backfill. A write still needs the primary. _bulk, _update, update-by-query, and native /v1 ingest do not route or replicate. Search does not merge aggregations, suggest, collapse, rescore, profile, search_after, or scroll across owners. Unscoped /_search, comma lists, and wildcards stay on the node that received them. The server does not open FileRaftLog, so a restart drops the in-memory plan. A replica removed from the in-sync set stays out for the life of the process.

A semantic query over a wildcard skips an index that has no semantic_text field of that name (#2308). Wildcard, _all, *, and alias expansion used to run the query on every concrete index, and one index without that field answered HTTP 400 and discarded the hits that could have been returned. Those expanded indices are now skipped. They contribute no hits. The request stays HTTP 200, _shards.failed counts them, and _shards.failures names the index and the engine reason. An index you named explicitly, including one name in a comma list, still fails the whole request with HTTP 400. If every searched index is skipped, the request is still HTTP 400. The default embedder on a semantic_text field is lexical feature-hashing unless the node was started with --embed-mode neural.

06 · UPGRADE

Install v1.0.0-rc.99

The installers download a GitHub release and check its SHA-256. Pin this release with XERJ_VERSION. On Linux, macOS, and Windows Git Bash, MSYS, and Cygwin:

$ curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | XERJ_VERSION=v1.0.0-rc.99 sh
$ export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
$ xerj --version

That sh installer writes ~/.local/bin (xerj.exe on Windows) and does not edit your shell profile. PowerShell writes a different directory and adds it to the user PATH. Open a new terminal after it:

> $env:XERJ_VERSION='v1.0.0-rc.99'; irm https://xerj.org/get.ps1 | iex

Re-run the installer you used last time. The two do not share a directory. xerj --version should print v1.0.0-rc.99. The longer matrix, the manual checksum block, and the musl-versus-gnu choice are on the install page.
